question: The range of the real valued function $f(x)= \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1+x^2}{2x}\right) + \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$ is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2024 Shift 2]

solution: Solution: First determine the domain of $f$ . The argument of $\sin^{-1}$ must satisfy $\left|\frac{1+x^2}{2x}\right|\le 1$ . Let $a=\frac{1+x^2}{2x}=\frac12\left(x+\frac1x\right)$ for $x\ne0$ . For $x>0$ , AM-GM gives $x+\frac1x\ge2$ , so $a\ge1$ . For $x<0$ , $x+\frac1x\le-2$ , so $a\le-1$ . Thus $|a|\le1$ can occur only when $|a|=1$ , so $x=1$ or $x=-1$ . At $x=1$ , $f(1)=\sin^{-1}(1)+\cos^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}+0=\frac{\pi}{2}$ . At $x=-1$ , $f(-1)=\sin^{-1}(-1)+\cos^{-1}(-1)=-\frac{\pi}{2}+\pi=\frac{\pi}{2}$ . Therefore the range is $\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$ . Hence option A is correct. © examsnet.com

At $x=-\frac{1}{2}$ , $f(x)=\frac{5}{2}$ , which is the minimum value of the function. As $x\to -\infty$ or $x\to \infty$ , $f(x)\to \infty$ . Hence the range is $\left[\frac{5}{2},\infty\right)$ , which equals the given codomain, so the function is onto. It is not one-one because $f\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)=5$ and $f(2)=5$ , while $-\frac{4}{3}\ne 2$ . Therefore, the function is onto but not one-one. © examsnet.com

question: If $n$ is an integer and $Z=\cos \theta + i \sin \; \theta, \theta \neq (2n+1) \; \frac{\pi}{2'}$ , then $\; \frac{1+Z^{2n}}{1-Z^{2n}} =$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2024 Shift 2]

solution: Solution: Since $Z=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta=e^{i\theta}$ , we have $Z^{2n}=e^{i2n\theta}$ . Using $1+e^{i\alpha}=2\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}e^{i\alpha/2}$ and $1-e^{i\alpha}=-2i\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}e^{i\alpha/2}$ with $\alpha=2n\theta$ gives: $1+Z^{2n}=2\cos(n\theta)e^{in\theta}$ and $1-Z^{2n}=-2i\sin(n\theta)e^{in\theta}$ . Therefore, $\frac{1+Z^{2n}}{1-Z^{2n}}=\frac{2\cos(n\theta)e^{in\theta}}{-2i\sin(n\theta)e^{in\theta}}$ Cancelling $e^{in\theta}$ and $2$ , we get: $\frac{1+Z^{2n}}{1-Z^{2n}}=\frac{\cos(n\theta)}{-i\sin(n\theta)}$ Since $\frac{1}{-i}=i$ , this becomes: $\frac{1+Z^{2n}}{1-Z^{2n}}=i\cot(n\theta)$ Hence the correct option is $i\cot n\theta$ .
